front_blocks.md: One mole of any element has a mass equal to its relative atomic mass in grams.

front_blocks.md: How many molecules are in 1 mole of H<sub>2</sub>, and how many individual H atoms does this correspond to?

back_blocks.md: 1 mole of H<sub>2</sub> contains **6.02 × 10**<sup>**23**</sup> molecules. Since each molecule has 2 H atoms, this corresponds to 2 × 6.02 × 10<sup>23</sup> = **1.204 × 10**<sup>**24**</sup> H atoms.

front_blocks.md: What is the mass of 1 mole of NaCl? (A<sub>r</sub>: Na = 23.0, Cl = 35.5)

back_blocks.md: Mass = 23.0 + 35.5 = **58.5 g mol**<sup>**-1**</sup>. The molar mass is found by summing the relative atomic masses of all atoms in the formula unit.

back_blocks.md: 1 mole of NaCl contains **1.204 × 10**<sup>**24**</sup> atoms in total, because each formula unit has one Na atom and one Cl atom, giving 2 × 6.02 × 10<sup>23</sup> atoms.
